item.title: Xi sends congratulatory letter to high-level dialogue marking 5th anniversary of GDI
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-26
BEIJING, Sept. 26 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has sent a congratulatory letter to a high-level dialogue marking the fifth anniversary of the Global Development Initiative (GDI) held at the UN headquarters in New York on Friday. Development is the eternal theme of human society and is key to promoting the well-being of humankind, Xi said. Xi recalled that he proposed the GDI at the UN General Assembly five years ago to advance global development cooperation, reinvigorate the global development cause, and help accelerate the implementation of the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Over the past five years, with the joint efforts of all parties, the GDI has been widely implemented, with cooperation projects under the initiative taking root and yielding outcomes in more than 120 countries, writing a new chapter of common development and win-win cooperation, Xi noted. Xi pointed out that nowadays, changes unseen in a century are accelerating across the world, and people in all countries are more keen about development. As the world's largest developing country and a member of the Global South, China stands ready to work with all parties to uphold a people-centered development philosophy, advance the GDI, turn the vision of the sustainable development goals into reality, and make new and greater contributions to building a community with a shared future for humanity, Xi said.

item.title: China and the United States reach eight deliverables and understandings
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-26
WASHINGTON, Sept. 26 -- From Sept. 23 to 25 local time, Chinese President Xi Jinping paid a state visit to the United States. During the visit, the two heads of state had in-depth discussions on the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability and major international and regional issues, and reached eight deliverables and understandings: 1. The two sides agree to build "a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity." 2. China and the United States support each other in successfully hosting the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting and the G20 Summit. The two heads of state intend to attend each other's meetings. 3. The two heads of state agree that Iran should honor its commitment to not developing nuclear weapons, and no country or institution can be allowed to impose tolls on international waterways. 4. The two heads of state recall that China and the U.S. were allies in World War II and fought side by side to win the war. 5. The two heads of state recognize the positive role of the China-U.S. economic and trade consultation mechanism, endorse the outcomes of the consultations between the two economic and trade teams, including establishing and taking forward the Board of Trade and other mechanisms, reaching an arrangement for a 30-billion-U.S.-dollar reciprocal tariff reduction, and the extension of the outcomes of economic and trade consultations in Kuala Lumpur, and give instructions that they be implemented. 6. The two sides note that cooperation between the counter-narcotics and law enforcement agencies of China and the U.S. has produced visible outcomes. Recently, the two sides working closely together have jointly cracked multiple cases involving New Psychoactive Substances (NPS) and precursor chemicals, and apprehended dozens of relevant criminal suspects in the two countries. 7. The two sides agree on the establishment of the China-U.S. AI Dialogue to exchange views on risks and benefits related to AI. The next exchange will occur in November 2026. China and the U.S. also agree to establish a bilateral communication channel for AI incidents. 8. The United States welcomes the arrival of two giant pandas, leased by China to Zoo Atlanta. In addition, the Chinese and U.S. militaries agree to conclude a memorandum of understanding on crisis communication and prevention as soon as possible, and continue their cooperation to search for the remains of missing U.S. servicemembers in China.

item.title: China, U.S. agree on constructive strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-26
WASHINGTON, Sept. 25 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday agreed to build a constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity. The consensus was reached during a tea chat at the White House attended by Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, and Trump and his wife, Melania Trump. Xi said the trip to Washington was his first state visit to the United States in 11 years. During the visit, the two sides added new substance to the vision for the China-U.S. relationship, and agreed to jointly build a constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity, Xi said. The two sides also achieved mutually beneficial outcomes in the economic and trade fields, which will be welcomed by the people of both countries and the international community, he added. Stressing that the future of China-U.S. relations is bright, Xi said that it reflects the trend of history. The road to a bright future is often winding, with difficulties and challenges bound to arise along the way, Xi said, adding that it is in line with the laws governing the development of things. Xi said he is willing to work with Trump to write a new chapter in the history of China-U.S. relations with the courage and a sense of responsibility to history. Calling Xi's state visit to the United States constructive and very successful, Trump said that the two sides held in-depth exchanges on U.S.-China relations and major international and regional issues, achieving positive outcomes that will benefit both countries. He said he looks forward to maintaining close contact with Xi and jointly guiding the development of U.S.-China relations. After the tea chat, Xi and Peng, accompanied by Trump and Melania, visited the U.S. National Archives. They walked together into the central hall, where they were briefed on the National Archives and its exhibits. The archives carry the wisdom of the forebears and offer insights for the future, Xi said, adding that over the past 250 years, the American people have pursued the American Dream and built a prosperous country and a beautiful home on the North American continent. The Chinese people, inheriting 5,000 years of Chinese civilization, have continued to make new achievements on the new journey toward realizing the Chinese Dream of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, Xi said. As two distinctive countries, China and the United States have different histories and cultures, social systems and development paths, Xi said. However, the people of the two countries share the same aspiration for a better life despite the differences, he said. If the two countries recognize and respect their differences, deepen mutual understanding and learn from each other, seek the biggest common denominator, expand the list of areas for cooperation, and properly manage differences, China-U.S. relations will enjoy steady and sustained growth, Xi said.

item.title: Xi returns to Beijing after state visit to U.S.
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-26
BEIJING, Sept. 26 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping returned to Beijing on Saturday afternoon after concluding his state visit to the United States. Xi's entourage, including his wife Peng Liyuan, Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and director of the General Office of the CPC Central Committee, Wang Yi, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and foreign minister, and He Lifeng, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and vice premier, returned on the same flight.

item.title: China issues revised regulations on implementation of audit law
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
BEIJING, Sept. 24 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang has signed a State Council decree promulgating revised regulations on the implementation of the audit law. The revised regulations, which consist of 7 chapters and 64 articles, will take effect on Dec. 1. Highlighting the need to refine and improve audit supervision, the regulations specify the scope and content of audits over fiscal revenues and expenditures, and bring the management and use of state-owned resources into the scope of special audit investigations, among others. To ensure that audit work is free from interference, the regulations add provisions on a registration and reporting system for any unwarranted attempts to inquire about or interfere with audit matters. All departments of the State Council and local authorities at all levels shall strengthen overall coordination, oversee rectification of problems uncovered in audits, and establish and improve relevant systems.

item.title: Chinese premier meets Malaysian PM
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
HANGZHOU, Sept. 24 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Thursday met with Prime Minister of Malaysia Anwar Ibrahim in Hangzhou, the provincial capital of Zhejiang in east China. Noting that the Chinese President's state visit to Malaysia in April last year has ushered bilateral relations into a new "Golden 50 Years," Li said that maintaining close communication and sound collaboration adds certainty to the common development of the two countries. China is willing to work with Malaysia to promote the in-depth and substantive development of a high-level strategic community with a shared future to better benefit the people of both countries, Li said. Li noted that China is willing to further leverage complementary economic advantages with Malaysia, promote high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, focus on mega infrastructure projects such as the East Coast Rail Link, increase market connection and connectivity, improve trade between the two countries, deepen cooperation in emerging industries and strive to achieve a higher level of mutual benefit and win-win results. Anwar, who has attended the opening ceremonies of the WorldSkills Competition and the Global Digital Trade Expo in China, said Malaysia attaches great importance to the comprehensive strategic partnership with China, firmly adheres to the one-China policy, and is willing to work with China to implement the important consensus reached by the leaders of the two countries and deepen practical cooperation in areas such as infrastructure and artificial intelligence. Anwar expressed Malaysia's support for China's proposition of strengthening the governance of artificial intelligence, and highly commended China's role in promoting the improvement of global governance, safeguarding the legitimate rights and interests of the Global South, and promoting common prosperity of all countries as a responsible major country. Malaysia is willing to join hands with China to make greater contributions to regional and world peace and development, Anwar said.

item.title: China to ease market access, boost digital trade: Premier Li
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
HANGZHOU, Sept. 24 -- China will further ease market access and improve policies for cross-border e-commerce retail imports, Premier Li Qiang said Thursday, pledging to share opportunities in its market with other countries. Addressing the opening ceremony of the Fifth Global Digital Trade Expo in Hangzhou, east China's Zhejiang Province, Li said the rapid growth of digital trade had created new opportunities, but had also brought widening development gaps, new trade barriers and gaps in international rules into sharper focus. Li called for closer international cooperation to strengthen digital connectivity and advance the alignment and mutual recognition of standards. The international community should enhance North-South cooperation in the field of digital trade, and provide more support to developing countries in terms of technology, infrastructure and personnel training, he said. Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, and Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan, Adylbek Aleshovich Kasymaliev, also addressed the opening ceremony, which was attended by more than 1,200 representatives from nearly 50 countries and regions, as well as international organizations. The expo, an event dedicated to promoting digital trade and industrial cooperation, is running until Sept. 27, with artificial intelligence as its main theme. China's digital trade has expanded rapidly in recent years. The country's digitally deliverable service trade value expanded at an average annual rate of 11.2 percent between 2016 and 2025, outpacing the global average by 1.8 percentage points.

item.title: China, Kazakhstan vow to deepen pragmatic cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
BEIJING, Sept. 22 -- Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang met with Kazakhstan's First Deputy Prime Minister Nurlybek Nalibayev in Beijing on Tuesday afternoon, and both sides agreed to deepen pragmatic cooperation. Ding, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said China and Kazakhstan are good neighbors, good friends and good partners linked by mountains and rivers and sharing a common future. In July this year, the two heads of state held a meeting, charting the course for the development of bilateral relations and the deepening of practical cooperation, Ding said. "As co-chairs of the China-Kazakhstan cooperation committee, we should fully implement the important common understandings reached by the two heads of state, give full play to the committee's role in overall coordination, and promote new outcomes in practical cooperation in key areas such as trade and investment, artificial intelligence and green minerals, so as to better enhance the well-being of the two peoples," Ding said. Nalibayev said Kazakhstan is willing to follow the strategic guidance of the two heads of state and work with China to further develop close and fruitful cooperation and bring Kazakhstan-China relations to a higher level.
